Welcome to the new home of WHS Fantasy Football

I've been running this league for over a decade now, so it was finally time to drag it into one place — every value, every rule, every dollar, every season we've ever played, all in one spot. Bookmark it. Actually use it this time.

Quick refresher for anyone who's forgotten (looking at you): this is a laid-back league of 12 high school buddies who still can't quit each other. It's an excuse to talk trash and stay in each other's business for four months a year. The goal is always to have fun — nobody's taking this too seriously. (Except the guy who just lost. He's taking it very seriously.)

We're a keeper league. Hang on to your guys from last year at a discount, so drafting well — and actually hitting on a sleeper for once — pays off for years, not just one Sunday. The full breakdown, Puka Nacua example included, lives in The Keeper Rules tab.

The money: there's a weekly payout for the top score, so it pays to stay locked in every single week, not just the weeks your team's actually good. Whatever's left after the weeklies splits 60% to 1st, 25% to 2nd, 15% to 3rd. The exact numbers are right below — go see how much you're chasing.

And no, there's no sacko punishment. Blame Yi for that. Instead, our last-place finishers get enshrined forever on the Hall of Fame tab's Sacko Wall, for permanent, public mockery. Play to the bitter end, or the wall gets you.

Keeper Values — who costs what this year. Find your name, check your damage, and follow the steps at the bottom to lock your two in on Yahoo.

How to actually set your keepers

Picking them here doesn't count — this page just tells you what everyone costs. You have to enter them in Yahoo yourself, and they're due Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 12:00 AM PDT. It takes about thirty seconds:

  1. Hover “My Team” in the top nav of our league, and pick Keepers from the dropdown that appears.
  2. Tick the checkbox next to the two players you want. Two is the max — one or none is allowed, three is not. Anyone showing a salary of 0 is ineligible this year and can't be kept no matter what; the number beside each name is what he costs you in the draft.
  3. Click “Set Keepers” at the bottom. Nothing is saved until you do. Go back in afterward and check they stuck — you can change your mind as many times as you like right up to the deadline.

Diagrams, not screenshots — Yahoo moves things around every couple of years, but the three steps have stayed put.

The Keeper Rules

Two keepers each, every keeper costs a pick — here's the whole system, no fine print:

  • Keep up to two players from your end-of-season roster. One or none is fine too.
  • The price is the round you drafted him in. Draft a guy in round 3, and keeping him costs your round-3 pick.
  • Drafted in round 8 or later — or picked up during the season? He costs a round 8. That's the sleeper discount: Puka Nacua went in round 14 back in 2023 and cost just an 8th to keep.
  • The price climbs one round for every year you keep him. An 8th becomes a 7th, a 7th becomes a 6th. Great picks get pricier to hold — that's the point.
  • Three years, then back in the pool. Draft year plus two keeps is the max — that's why Puka finally hit the board again. A trade restarts the clock for the new owner; the price stays put.
  • First-rounders can't be kept. And once a keeper's price climbs all the way to round 1, his run is over.
  • The price sticks to the player. Dropping and re-adding a guy doesn't make him cheap again — and if you drop him and never take him back, he can't be kept at all.
  • He has to finish the year on your team — and he has to have played. Rostered the final four weeks of the season, with at least one game played that year. No stashing December pickups, no keeping a guy who never took the field.
  • Your two keepers can't cost the same round. One bumps up a round — your choice, or ADP decides for you.
  • In Yahoo: the salary next to a player's name is his price in rounds. A 0 means he can't be kept this year; no number means 8.
